submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on structural/boundary tokens rather than content: strongest (about 0.85-1.0 of max) on whitespace control characters (\t, \r, \x0c, \n) that follow a sentence- or statement-ending '.' or ';', next on commas and bare '\n' (about 0.55-0.7), weaker on '.', '?' and short function words (the, and, that, is: about 0.2-0.6), and essentially zero on content words (nouns, adjectives, most verbs). Activation is largest near the start of a text and decays somewhat over long contexts.
